disease_label_per_paper: Placental abruption leading to disseminated intravascular coagulation at 21 weeks gestation
presentation_summary: 25-year-old primigravida initially presented at 21 weeks gestation with abdominal pain and vaginal spotting.
A live fetus was seen on initial ultrasound and no abruption was reported, but laboratory findings showed DIC.
At transfer she had worsening abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding; vitals included pulse 70/min, blood pressure 100/55 mmHg, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air.
Bedside ultrasound at the tertiary unit showed fetal demise and large collections presumed to be blood clot.
Uterine evacuation delivered a stillborn fetus and a 1300 mL adherent clot, confirming placental abruption as the trigger.

course_observations.description: Received packed red cells, fibrinogen-rich cryoprecipitate, fresh frozen plasma, and platelets; coagulopathy initially did not improve before transfer.
After cervical preparation and delivery, fundal massage rapidly evacuated a 1300 mL clot adherent to the placental surface; total blood loss was 2000 mL.
Platelets recovered to 183 x10^9/L and hemoglobin stabilized after uterine evacuation and transfusion support.
